title: World War II
subtitle: Six years that remade the world, from a Polish border to a Japanese city

stops.narration: The war begins here. German troops cross the Polish frontier on 1 September 1939, and Britain and France declare war two days later.
With France fallen, the fighting moves to the sky over southern England, where the RAF denies the Luftwaffe the air superiority an invasion would need.
In June 1941 Hitler turns east and invades his own ally, opening the vast front where most of the war's dead would fall.
Six months later Japanese carriers strike the Pacific Fleet at anchor, and a European war becomes a global one.
On 6 June 1944 the Allies come back to France across five Normandy beaches, opening the second front Stalin had demanded for years.
The war ends in August 1945 with two atomic bombs, and the world enters the nuclear age it still lives in.

title: World War I
subtitle: From two shots in Sarajevo to the silence of the eleventh hour

stops.narration: A teenage nationalist kills an archduke on a Sarajevo street corner, and within five weeks the alliance system has pulled Europe into war.
East of Paris the French and British stop the German advance, and the war of movement freezes into a line of trenches from the sea to Switzerland.
The Allies try to break the deadlock by attacking the Ottomans at the Dardanelles, and spend eight months on the cliffs before giving up.
At Verdun the strategy becomes attrition for its own sake, with some 700,000 men killed or wounded over ten months of shelling.
American entry in April 1917 brings the manpower and industry that will decide the Western Front the following year.
In a railway carriage at Compiègne the guns are stopped at eleven o'clock on 11 November 1918, leaving ten million soldiers dead.

title: Rise and fall of Rome
subtitle: Twelve centuries from a village on the Tiber to an empty throne at Ravenna

stops.narration: Tradition puts the founding of the city at 753 BC, a cluster of settlements on hills above a ford in the Tiber.
Rome's wars with Carthage, beginning in 264 BC, turn an Italian republic into the master of the western Mediterranean.
In 49 BC Caesar leads a legion across a small river into Italy, and the Republic never recovers.
Augustus keeps the republican forms and takes the power, beginning two centuries of relative peace across the Mediterranean.
Constantine moves the centre of gravity east in 330, founding a Christian capital on the Bosphorus that will outlive Rome by a thousand years.
In 476 a Germanic commander deposes the last western emperor at Ravenna and sends the imperial insignia to Constantinople.

title: The Mongol Empire
subtitle: From a council on the Onon river to the largest land empire ever assembled

stops.narration: In 1206 the steppe tribes acclaim Temüjin as Genghis Khan, uniting them under one law and one decimal army.
The sack of the Jin capital in 1215 proves that the Mongols can take walled cities, not merely raid the countryside.
Hulagu's army destroys Baghdad in 1258 and kills the last Abbasid caliph, ending five centuries of the caliphate.
Two years later the Mamluks of Egypt stop the Mongols in Galilee, the first real check on their westward advance.
Kublai declares the Yuan dynasty in 1271 and rules China from Dadu, ruling as emperor rather than as a conquering khan.
In 1368 a peasant rebel takes Dadu and founds the Ming, and the Mongol court retreats to the steppe it came from.

title: Age of Exploration
subtitle: A century and a half in which the sea routes of the world were joined

stops.narration: Ming China sends the largest fleets in the world across the Indian Ocean from 1405, then abandons the voyages entirely.
In 1488 Bartolomeu Dias is blown past the tip of Africa and shows Portugal that the Atlantic and Indian Oceans join.
Sailing west for Castile, Columbus reaches the Bahamas in October 1492 and permanently links two hemispheres.
Six years later Vasco da Gama anchors at Calicut, and Portugal begins seizing the spice trade by force.
The Magellan expedition sails from Spain in 1519; three years later eighteen survivors return, having gone all the way round.
Cook charts Australia's east coast in 1770, filling in one of the last great blanks on the European map of the world.

title: Cold War and decolonisation
subtitle: Two superpowers, dozens of new flags, and the world of 1991

stops.narration: In August 1947 the largest colony of all becomes two states, and ten to twenty million people cross a line drawn weeks earlier.
The Soviets cut off West Berlin in 1948 and the West flies in coal and food for eleven months, hardening the division of Europe.
Ghana's independence in 1957 under Nkrumah opens the wave that frees most of Africa within a decade.
Thirteen days in October 1962 bring the superpowers closer to nuclear war than at any other moment.
On the evening of 9 November 1989 the guards open the gates, and the wall that defined the Cold War comes down.
On 26 December 1991 the Soviet Union dissolves into fifteen states, and the contest that shaped half a century is over.

title: The ancient world
subtitle: From the first kings of the Nile and Euphrates to Alexander's conquest of Persia

stops.narration: Around 3000 BC the Nile valley becomes one kingdom, and history, in the sense of written records, begins.
In Uruk, accountants pressing reeds into clay invent writing.
Sargon of Akkad conquers the Sumerian cities and builds the first empire.
Hammurabi of Babylon carves his laws in stone for everyone to see.
Egypt and the Hittites clash at Kadesh, then sign the oldest surviving peace treaty.
Around 1177 BC the interconnected Bronze Age world collapses within a generation.
From its ruins comes the Phoenician alphabet, ancestor of most scripts in use today.
Cyrus the Great takes Babylon and founds the largest empire yet seen.
The Greeks turn back the Persians at sea off Salamis.
A century and a half later Alexander destroys the Persian Empire at Gaugamela.

title: The scientific journey
subtitle: How people learned to measure the Earth, map the heavens and read the code of life

stops.narration: In Ptolemaic Alexandria, the Library gathers the knowledge of the Mediterranean world.
Using shadows and geometry, Eratosthenes measures the size of the Earth.
In Gupta India, Aryabhata argues that the Earth spins on its axis.
Baghdad's scholars translate the Greeks and invent algebra.
Gutenberg's press makes knowledge cheap to copy.
Copernicus moves the Earth out of the centre of the universe.
Galileo's telescope shows moons circling Jupiter.
Newton's laws tie the falling apple to the orbiting Moon.
Darwin explains the diversity of life by natural selection.
A patent clerk in Bern rewrites physics in a single year.
In Cambridge, the double helix reveals how life copies itself.
And in 1969 humans walk on the Moon.

title: The age of revolutions
subtitle: A century of uprisings that replaced kings with citizens

stops.narration: In 1688 Parliament replaces England's king and sets limits on royal power.
In 1776 thirteen colonies declare that all men are created equal.
In 1789 Paris rises and the French Revolution begins.
In 1791 the enslaved people of Saint-Domingue rise and create the first free Black republic.
Napoleon, the Revolution's heir, falls at Waterloo in 1815.
Bolívar's armies free northern South America from Spain.
In 1848 revolution sweeps Europe from Paris to Budapest.

title: The Silk Roads
subtitle: Two thousand years of trade, ideas and disease across Eurasia

stops.narration: Han envoy Zhang Qian travels west and opens official contact with Central Asia.
Tang Chang'an becomes the cosmopolitan eastern terminus of the routes.
At Talas, Abbasid and Tang armies meet, and papermaking travels west.
Baghdad translates the knowledge carried along the routes.
The Mongols unite the steppe and, for a time, make the whole route safe to travel.
A Venetian merchant sets out for the court of Kublai Khan.
The same routes carry the Black Death west to Europe.
Ming treasure fleets take the maritime Silk Road as far as East Africa.
